title: ALMA beneath the stars
caption: ALMA antennas under the Milky Way, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A group of 12-meter dish antennas turn toward targets in the night sky, as the Milky Way crosses the picture through a field of countless stars. The antennas belong to the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, ALMA, and this is only a part of the array.

ALMA's dishes work very differently from the camera that recorded this scene. They are tuned to light at millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths, far longer than the visible light our eyes and ordinary cameras detect. By combining signals from many antennas, the array can behave like a single much larger telescope.

Above them, the Milky Way appears as a luminous band, the combined light of countless distant stars in the disc of our galaxy, with darker patches where dust blocks the view. This photograph by A. Duro sets the antennas, turned toward their targets, beside the galaxy stretched above them.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at ALMA. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would in person.
